gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about pushchairs in the show rules. The paddocks and car parks are grass, so I would bring one with sturdy wheels and ask Shuttleworth before you go if you’re unsure. Baby changing is in the Visitor Centre and the hangar toilets.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Well behaved dogs on leads are welcome on the airfield paddocks, but not in the hangars, the main café, the Swiss Garden or Shuttleworth House. Dogs aren’t allowed at all at the Flying Proms because of the pyrotechnics.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You’re welcome to bring your own food and drink, but no barbecues, sharp knives or glass bottles. Shuttleworth can take away any alcohol you bring in, so I would leave it at home and buy a drink on site.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Gazebos and oversized umbrellas aren’t allowed, but a well tethered beach tent up to 1.2m high is fine. Ladders are banned too. Folding chairs aren’t on the banned list, but I couldn’t see windbreaks mentioned, so I would check before you pack one.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about free water refills on show days. I would bring plenty to drink and a refillable bottle, and ask at the Visitor Centre on the day.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: I couldn’t see a Changing Places toilet listed. There are accessible toilets at the Visitor Centre, the Runway Café, between Hangars 3 and 4 and in the Swiss Garden, so I would ask the team before you go if you need one.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: Carers of disabled visitors get a free ticket alongside the paid ticket for the person they look after, booked by emailing enquiries@shuttleworth.org. Random spot checks happen on the day, so bring your paperwork.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about hearing loops or BSL at the air shows. I would ask Shuttleworth before you go, so they know what would help on the day.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s no quiet room listed for show days. The Swiss Garden is calmer and shady, which may work for you if someone needs a break, although dogs can’t go in. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a re-entry rule for show days. With the holding queue and stewarded car parks, I would ask a steward before you head back out to the car.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: The first aid point isn’t shown before the day, but the site map emailed out before the big shows should help. I would agree a meeting point like a hangar number, and tell the nearest steward straight away if you get separated.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. Vintage aircraft are fussy about wind and rain, and tickets aren’t refunded even if a show is called off, unless you bought ticket protection.

days.html:
Pick Your Show

Shuttleworth has seven air shows in 2027, and each one has its own theme. Most open at 09:00 with the flying from about 14:00, and most have a second display in the evening as the light softens. Have a think about who’s coming and how late you want to stay, then try the picker below.

Shows in 2027Seven
Season9 May to 25 September
Under 18sFree, apart from the Flying Proms
CampingAt every show

May To July

Season PremiereSunday 9 May. Gates 09:00 to 18:00, with one display from about 14:00 to 17:30. Tickets from £35.
Military Air ShowSaturday 29 May. Military aircraft, vehicles and history, plus a Military Camp. Displays from about 14:00 and again at 19:30.
Festival Of FlightSaturday 26 and Sunday 27 June. The flagship show. Gates 09:00 to 21:00, with an evening display from about 20:00.
Summer Air ShowSaturday 24 July. Going all American for the 80th anniversary of the US Air Force. Displays from about 14:00 and 19:30.

August And September

Wings And WheelsSaturday 14 August. Aircraft overhead and classic, modern and film cars on the ground. Displays from about 14:00 and 19:00.
Flying PromsSaturday 28 August. Aerobatics with the National Symphony Orchestra playing live. Gates 10:00 to 22:00, flying about 18:30 to 20:00.
Season FinaleSaturday 25 September. Brand new for 2027, with an evening display and fireworks from 19:50.

Who’s coming?

What are you after?

How late do you want to stay?

Bringing the dog?

I Would Pick The Season Premiere

  1. WhyIt’s the first flying of the year, on a Sunday in May, and there’s just the one display, so you’re home before dark. This may work for you with little ones who won’t last into the evening.
  2. Good to knowGates are 09:00 to 18:00 and the display runs from about 14:00 to 17:30. The fun fair, Discovery Zones, vintage bus rides and the Swiss Garden are all included, so I would use the morning for those.
  3. Getting thereParking is free, and every show uses the Alder Drive entrance. More in .

I Would Pick The Military Air Show

  1. WhyIf wartime aircraft and military history are your thing, this one is built around them, with a Military Camp on the ground and a tribute to those who have served.
  2. Good to knowThere’s an armed forces rate for serving and ex forces personnel, and ID may be checked on the day. The second display runs from about 19:30 to 20:30, so pack a jumper if you’re staying.
  3. Getting thereFree parking through Alder Drive. More in .

I Would Pick The Festival Of Flight

  1. WhyThis is Shuttleworth’s flagship weekend and the biggest show of their year. If you only go to one, I would make it this.
  2. Good to knowGates are 09:00 to 21:00, with the main display from about 14:00 and an evening one from about 20:00, both still to be confirmed. Camping is offered, and this is one of only two shows with showers on the campsite.
  3. Getting thereRooms near the A1 go quickly this weekend, so I would book early. More in .

I Would Pick The Summer Air Show

  1. WhyIt’s in the school holidays, and for 2027 it’s going all American to mark 80 years of the US Air Force. Children love to see the aircraft parked on the grass between flights.
  2. Good to knowThe first display runs from about 14:00 to 18:30 and the second from about 19:30 to 20:30. The ground attractions open with the gates at 09:00, so there’s plenty to fill the morning.
  3. Getting thereFree parking through Alder Drive. More in .

I Would Pick Wings And Wheels

  1. WhyIf someone in your group is more into cars than aircraft, this is the one. There’s a Pit Stop Paddock with movie cars and racing simulators, plus a BMX stunt show.
  2. Good to knowIt’s only the second year of this show. Gates are 09:00 to 20:00, with displays from about 14:00 to 18:00 and again from about 19:00 to 20:00.
  3. Getting thereFree parking through Alder Drive. More in .

I Would Pick The Flying Proms

  1. WhyIt’s a proper evening out, with aerobatics and the National Symphony Orchestra playing live. I think it suits a couple or a group of friends with a picnic.
  2. Good to knowTickets are from £62.50, and children aged 4 and over pay £22. Gates open at 10:00 and the flying runs from about 18:30 to 20:00. Dogs aren’t allowed at this one.
  3. Getting thereIt finishes late, so if you’re on the shuttle bus, check your return time. More in .

I Would Pick The Season Finale

  1. WhyIt’s brand new for 2027 and closes the season with flying, family entertainment and a fireworks display to finish. What would happen if you stayed to the very end? You’d see the old aircraft in the last light, then the fireworks.
  2. Good to knowGates are 09:00 to 20:00. The main display runs from about 14:00 to 18:00, the second from about 19:00 to 19:30 and the fireworks start at 19:50. Late September evenings can be fresh, so bring layers.
  3. Getting thereFree parking through Alder Drive. More in .
Jack’s tipCamping is offered at every 2027 show, at £27.50 a pitch a night for one to five nights, Wednesday to Sunday. The pitch includes entry to the Collection and the Swiss Garden, so if you’re coming a long way, this might work for your family. You add it when you book your show tickets.
Official siteAll seven 2027 shows, tickets and camping

Times and prices may change for 2027. Display times are approximate, and Shuttleworth doesn’t publish times for each aircraft.
